Rifampin increases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Fexinidazole decreases the levels or effects of rifampin by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 3. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fexofenadine through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of finasteride by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of flibanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially reduce systemic exposure to flibanserin. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Rifampin reduces the levels of fluconazole by increasing its metabolism. Conversely, fluconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 8. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by both P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of flurazepam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of flurbiprofen by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 11. Rifampin increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through mechanisms that are not fully understood. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 13. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fostamatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fostemsavir (a prodrug) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, as it may lead to a loss of virologic response and resistance. 15. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of frovatriptan by altering CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 16. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fruquintinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ganaxolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose, but do not exceed the maximum daily dose for the patient’s weight. 18. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of gefitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer, increase the gefitinib dose to 500 mg daily. Resume the standard dose of 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the inducer. 19. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of gentamicin through the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of geprione by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
